scope: Read-only capacity-source review; no dispatch, browser, API spend, secrets, product-health verdict, or repository edit.

reality_first.observed: Member runs 39354133238 and 39359003772 reached CPU_PENDING at 100% busy on four logical CPUs; the latter then hit 84% busy and a terminal resource-invalid final before Chat. A successful guest comparison also spiked to 100% then recovered. The current T08 no-signal Scrape route is B/guest/development-artifact only; the driver runs a title-only localhost page, requests headed Chrome, verifies a SIDE_PANEL target, uses a trusted Playwright click, and captures CDP screenshots. The existing guard refuses non-Darwin hosts.

requirements: initial B-only guest no-signal T08 scope and frozen artifact
normal CLI and direct workflow refusal of broader Linux tuples
unchanged Mac refusal thresholds and timing
Linux CPU, memory, pressure, load, swap and disk measurement
real headed Chrome and side-panel proof
at most two hosted lanes and 15-minute bound
workflow cost registry and real spend gate
separate source, pilot and product verdicts

blocking.finding: The plan calls for a live window and visible pane but does not make X11 display visibility an acceptance predicate. Current native screenshots are Page.captureScreenshot from CDP targets, while observePanelVisibility is optional and a failed native-window lookup is recorded as measured:false. Thus a headed Chromium with a SIDE_PANEL target could produce passing target screenshots even if its Xvfb window is unmapped, hidden, or the side panel is not present in the displayed browser frame.
blocking.fix: Freeze an explicit Linux pass oracle before build: prove the owned browser has a mapped, non-minimized X11 window on its private DISPLAY; capture the X display/window pixels showing the selected native side panel and correlate them with the owned Chrome window and SIDE_PANEL target. Missing mapping, display screenshot, or correlation must refuse native credit. Keep CDP screenshots as additional detail. Add a targeted mutation where CDP target screenshots succeed while the window is unmapped and assert failure.

blocking.finding: The plan requires a Linux pressure reading and an independently reviewed conservative criterion, but does not state the source, sampling window, numeric unsafe boundary, or how it maps to the existing pressureLevel=1 normal verdict. The shared reasons() function currently treats any pressureLevel other than 1 as unsafe. Leaving the translation to implementation allows a permissive mapping that silently changes host refusal while all unchanged CPU/memory thresholds appear intact.
blocking.fix: Specify the exact Linux kernel pressure source and conservative unsafe rule in the frozen route contract, including sample window, malformed/unavailable refusal, and typed journal representation. Review that rule independently against captured healthy and pressured samples, then prove a forced-pressure mutation blocks admission and active work without altering the Mac branch.

verdict_limit: This evaluates feasibility and false-pass boundaries of a capacity plan; it says nothing about current product health or future Ubuntu pilot outcome.
